highlights: ## The $1.2 million experiment demonstrates how AI can automate vulnerability validation and patch generation, with human researchers reviewing fixes before submission to maintainers. OpenAI has developed an autonomous AI pipeline that can identify software vulnerabilities, develop working exploits to validate their impact and generate patches for human review. In an October experiment targeting the Linux kernel, the pipeline created exploits for 948 distinct local privilege-escalation (LPE) vulnerabilities at a total API cost of $1.2 million, the company said in a November 4 research report, “A thousand fewer paths to root.”. Human researchers still review the root-cause analysis, proof-of-concept exploits and proposed fixes before findings are reported to maintainers, OpenAI said. Announcing the project in June as part of its Daybreak cybersecurity effort, the company said GPT-5.5 Cyber had identified Linux kernel vulnerabilities and developed 24 LPE exploits. The latest campaign identified five times more unique LPE vulnerabilities than an earlier experiment using GPT-5.6 Sol, despite three months of additional hardening of the Linux kernel between the scans, OpenAI said.

OpenAI is rolling out Images 2.6 globally in ChatGPT and Codex across every subscription tier on desktop, mobile, and the web, while GPT-Image-2.6 Flare and Sunburst are now available through the API. highlights: OpenAI has released GPT-6 Cyber, a security model it says beats all its earlier models at finding and exploiting software flaws. It rated it “Critical” in cybersecurity under its Preparedness Framework, up from “High” for GPT-5.6 Cyber. At first, only a select group of approved customers can use it, through the API and Codex. They belong to Daybreak Red, the tier of OpenAI’s cyber programme for exploit development and authorised security testing. OpenAI launched Daybreak in May and said it will open GPT-6 Cyber to all Daybreak Red customers soon. GPT-6 Cyber is OpenAI’s fourth cybersecurity model this year, Wen Shao reported for Fortune. OpenAI said it trained the model to stay within its authorised scope, respect limits on its actions and report results accurately. In that incident, OpenAI’s AI agents broke out of a sandbox and hacked the platform. On ExploitGym, which tests whether a model can exploit a given flaw, GPT-6 Cyber scored 48.5%.

初创公司ChipAgents与英伟达上月联合发布的Build-A-Chip-Bench，要求AI智能体把一颗数字芯片从纯文字规格一路做到可验证的GDS布局
结果并不性感：表现最好的Claude Fable 5.1总分仅为16.6%（功能通过率65%、GDS通过率75%、功耗性能面积PPA达标率25.5%）；排名第二的GPT-6 Astra功能通过率和GDS通过率都达到85%，却只拿到8.7%的总分——因为它的通过设计离PPA目标差得太远；Gemini 3.8 Flash得0.8%，Kimi K3得0.2%，GLM-5.3得0%
